title: Giotto AI License Bans Independent Performance Benchmarks
summary:
The user agreement for the new Giotto AI family requires written permission from the Swiss research lab before any user can reverse engineer the software or share independent performance evaluations. The restriction applies to the flagship Alto model and the smaller Solo version, which is optimized to run on a single GPU for private organizational infrastructure.

The licensing terms have drawn criticism from users who argue the restrictions contradict Giotto's claims that the tools are built for "sovereign AI" to help Europe control its own technology. Despite the ban on public testing, a leaked intelligence index from Artificial Analysis claims the models achieved high scores on the GPQA, AIME, and MATH-500 benchmarks.

Today we announce the launch of the Giotto family of models. We are unveiling Giotto Alto and Giotto Solo, the smartest European sovereign AI models on the market.

Giotto Alto is our flagship model built for advanced reasoning capabilities, free for everyone and available on the App Store and Google Play. It is hosted on European cloud infrastructure, so your data stays in Europe. Giotto Solo is the smartest model that runs on a single GPU, so organisations can keep their AI on their own infrastructure.

We are a Swiss lab with a European heart and we built this so that Europe can run advanced AI on its own terms.
